ideas.title: Fire that spreads through whatever it touches
ideas.critique: This is the round-1 hot-wire grass fire rebuilt so it answers that idea's weak spot: the heat lives in real props and parts, a fence weakens by char depth and sags, and wet fuel won't catch until it dries. That is a new general system and a fight the player can win or lose, and the friends have a reason to react. The risk is the radiation 'seen area' and the char-strength coupling getting cut down to a distance falloff and a timer, which would turn a fence collapse into a scripted break.

ideas.title: Catch the lightning
ideas.critique: A dielectric-breakdown bolt grown through a Laplace field that the player's own conductors shape, leaving a glass root you dig up next morning, is something nobody expects from a game, and the field solve is the kind the big goal needs. Play depends on a storm the player waits for and a strike that is over in a frame. Its look also depends on the heat system existing first; without it the bolt is pretty and nothing it hits stays changed.

ideas.title: A lamp that lasts the night
ideas.critique: A filament the player built, lighting the cottage with real blackbody light, is a direct road step and a good use of the path tracer. But a glowing object in the dark that lights what's around it is what the hot-glass still already showed, and picking filament, thickness and jar is the 'variants with different outcomes' recipe in another form. Oxygen used up by a candle and thinning that raises resistance are what would make it more than a lookup.

ideas.title: The eel in the pond is a battery
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: A living power source with moods, read through a field in a conductor, is a fresh cross between creature behaviour and the electricity road, and hunting with a real voltage that fish feel is more than an animation. Still, it is one more creature, and a single current dipole in a pond is a closed-form rig for one case. Wires picking up a voltage by where they lie is the interesting part; a lamp that flickers on cue would read as scripted.
